editorial.headline: Nationally Open New-Vehicle Wholesale, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans new cars and commercial vehicles, open nationally at every business scale but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today, even though it is nationally open to foreign investment. The activity is wholesale trade in new cars, with a scope extending beyond passenger vehicles to special cars such as ambulances, caravans, minibuses and fire engines. It also includes trucks, trailers, semi-trailers, goods vehicles and other motorised transport vehicles. In practical terms, it is a single wholesale activity spanning the new passenger, specialist and freight-carrying vehicles expressly named in its scope.

The registration field is broad in business-scale terms. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA and its foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, under the stated Perpres basis. A national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% does not create a PMA registration path in Bali. It establishes the national position for the activity; the Bali outcome is governed by a separate, explicitly recorded restriction.

In Bali, the result is unambiguous: the activity is marked BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO for PMA registration. The record attributes this to OSS risk at the Besar scale, where every scope is classified as Low or Medium-Low risk, bringing the activity within Bali’s moratorium from May 2026. That provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA, island-wide and permanently. There is no Bali-specific foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition recorded here; the barrier is the moratorium triggered by the stated risk classification.

The honest reading is therefore two-level. At the national level, this is an open PMA activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling and access across all four stated enterprise scales. In Bali, however, it is not an available PMA registration route. The national openness remains real, but it cannot be treated as permission to establish the activity through PMA on the island while the permanent, island-wide moratorium applies.
